memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So Joshua said to the Israelites: "How long will you wait before you begin to take possession of the land that the Lord, the God of your ancestors, has given you?" - Josh 18:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joshua's question cuts straight to the heart: "How long will you wait before you begin to take possession of the land?" Seven tribes had not yet claimed their inheritance. The land was there, given by God, but they were hesitating, delaying, failing to step forward and take hold of it. Joshua names the delay for what it is — a kind of unbelief that leaves God's gift unclaimed.

It is a striking thing. The land was already given by God's promise. The obstacle was not God's willingness but the people's slowness to act. They had grown passive, perhaps comfortable, perhaps fearful, and the gift sat waiting while they lingered. Joshua's question is meant to stir them: why wait any longer for what God has already granted?

The same question echoes into our own lives. God has given us so much in Christ — forgiveness to walk in, peace to enjoy, a calling to pursue, His presence to know. Yet how often we hesitate, leaving His gifts unclaimed, living far below what He has already provided. We wait for a better moment, a stronger feeling, a clearer sign, while the inheritance sits ready. Joshua's words are a loving challenge: how long will you wait? God's gifts in Christ are meant to be entered into now, by faith. Do not let them lie unclaimed.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What has God already given you in Christ that you have been slow to claim?
- Why do you think you hesitate — comfort, fear, waiting for a "better time"?
- What would it look like to stop waiting and step forward in faith today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, forgive me for leaving Your gifts unclaimed while I hesitate. Stir me to stop waiting and to step forward in faith into all You have already given me in Christ. Amen.
